gloss_en: COBie parameters mapped in Revit (Type Name, Component Name) are missing in IFC exported with the 'IFC 2x3 COBie 2.4 Design Deliverable' setup.
title_original: Cobie to IFC export issues
question_paraphrase: Mapped COBie data to Revit parameters, exported with COBie 2.4 Design Deliverable setup, but COBie type/component names are missing from the IFC; do not want to remap.
phrasing_notes: Newbie post, asks for help, offers to email model
answer_summary: Export IFC first, then extract COBie from the IFC; the endorsed COBie MVD is IFC4 so re-export as IFC4; Revit default IFC output is weak, audit IFC classes.

gloss_en: Do bridge deck items (wearing surface, kerbs, junction boxes) belong in IfcBridge/IfcBridgePart SUPERSTRUCTURE or in a separate IfcRoad?
title_original: Exporting bridge elements to IFC 4.3: IfcBridge or IfcRoad?
question_paraphrase: Should wearing surface, kerbs, junction boxes go inside the IfcBridge model or in a separate IfcRoad model, and are there criteria?
phrasing_notes: Concise, class names verbatim, no software named
answer_summary: Everything between approach slabs is bridge, except asphalt wearing course which is road pavement; kerbs, footpaths, drains, barriers are usually bridge.

gloss_en: Alignment exported as IFC 4x1 from ProVI imports into Civil 3D 2022 but nothing is visible even after Zoom Extents.
title_original: IFC 4x1 file containing alignment is not opening in Civil 3D
question_paraphrase: Highway project; exported alignment as IFC 4x1, import into Civil 3D 2022 completes but nothing shows, even zoom extents. Ground and corridor surfaces worked with IFC 2x3.
phrasing_notes: Short, cites exact versions, asks if anyone has done this
answer_summary: IFC 4.1 was withdrawn and never certified by bSI, so output is unreliable; raise with the vendor.

gloss_en: Looking for IFC 4.2/4.3 bridge sample files to test an IFC reading tool.

answer_summary: Pointers to the TPF-5(372) Unit Test Suite on GitHub, the ACCA Bridge-for-MINnD IFC4X3 model on bSI GitHub, bSI Validation Service compliance.

gloss_en: Beginner guide mapping building and bridge elements to IFC 4x3 classes and predefined types; follow-up on nested IfcBridgePart and US AASHTO-aligned hierarchy.

question_paraphrase: Shares a typelist mapping elements to IFC 4x3 classes/predefined types because bSDD makes them hard to find; later asks whether IfcBridgePart can nest and how.
phrasing_notes: Longer practitioner thread, mentions bSDD and class names
answer_summary: US bridge proposal aligned with AASHTO treats nested IfcBridgePart as best practice (spatial level plus semantic container); Bonsai breakdown is hard-coded for buildings.
